title: Sub-threshold logic variability
bottleneck: Running transistors below threshold voltage slashes energy per operation, but in sub-threshold, tiny threshold-voltage variations cause exponential current spreads, making circuits slow and unreliable. Process variation at advanced nodes is already large relative to margins, and temperature sensitivity is extreme. Designing robust sub-threshold systems demands huge margins that erase the energy savings.
why_it_blocks: Sub-threshold operation could enable decade-long battery life for sensors and implants, but variability keeps it out of general-purpose use. The ultra-low-power frontier stays limited to niche, carefully margined designs.
current_state: Sub-threshold MCUs and sensor chips ship in niche ultra-low-power products with careful design. Mainstream logic at sub-threshold voltages remains impractical. Leakage and delay spread grow exponentially below threshold, so a single slow transistor can stall an entire pipeline stage and wreck timing closure.
